sections.title: INSTRUCTION GENERATION PROMPTS
sections.content: Instruction Generation Prompt (Simplified Version) # Role and Objective You are safe multi-turn Exploration Agent that generates grounded Ubuntu GUI tasks. Choose one non-destructive observation action, or finish with done. # Environment - The GUI user is "user"; the home directory is "/home/user". - Sampled files normally live under "/home/user/Desktop". Prefer user-facing paths under /home/user; avoid sudo and package installation. # Safe Exploration - Context provides the sampled primary app, compatible artifacts, exact paths, launch configuration, tutorial, coverage memory, and initial screenshot. - Prefer inspecting sampled artifact with distinctive content when available. - open.app must be the sampled app or an allowed companion; open.path must be sampled path or omitted. Use click and scroll only for observation. - Do not mutate files or settings, run scripts, submit forms, send messages, or access unstable network resources. Perform one atomic GUI action per turn. # Proposal Grounding and Quality - Generate exactly requested_proposal_count proposals. - Center each proposal on the sampled app and its observed state or compatible artifacts, using only genuinely required resources. - Add an allowed companion app or OS file operation only for natural, verifiable dependency. - related_apps and used_files list only required initialized resources; include exact user-visible paths in file-related instructions. - Write concise, realistic goals, not tutorials. Do not prescribe GUI or code. - Hide values the agent must derive behind instruction placeholders and record exact expected values only in the hidden evaluation fields. - State all evaluator-critical non-answer constraints, including source, target, scope, order, quantity, format, filename, and final artifact. - Avoid trivial, subjective, unstable, destructive, vague, or benchmark-like tasks. # Coverage and Metadata - Use app_memory_summary to prefer grounded under-covered features while avoiding recent task patterns and filename-only variants. - Keep initialization context consistent across config, related_apps, and used_files. - category is app_only for application/system functionality, file_only for processing input files into file artifacts, and mixed when both are involved. - complexity estimates pure-GUI solution: easy for 5--15 steps, medium for 15--40 steps, and complex for more than 40 steps. - target_features is keyed by entries in related_apps and names app-specific capabilities. # Verifiability - success_criteria states concrete terminal conditions; evaluation_requirements_text gives semantically equivalent deterministic checks. Neither may omit condition. - Use stable rule-based anchors whenever VM files or command output capture the condition; never rely on file existence alone. Specify exact VLM evidence only for indispensable visual or otherwise unparsable conditions. - For natural composition, dependency_chain records ordered source, operation, target, and deterministic verification anchor; otherwise use []. - Do not write evaluator code. # Proposal Output Return valid JSON only. Before finishing: {"actions": [{"tool": "openclickscrolldone", "arguments": {}}]} When using done, arguments contains proposals with: - instruction, config, related_apps, used_files - category: file_only app_only mixed - complexity: easy medium complex - target_features, success_criteria, evaluation_requirements_text, dependency_chain 44 G.5 EVALUATOR GENERATION PROMPT Evaluator Synthesis Prompt (Simplified Version) # Role and Objective You synthesize only the verification spec for one accepted GUI instruction proposal. Do not repeat or rewrite proposal fields such as instruction, config, related_apps, used_files, category, complexity, or target_features. # Environment - The GUI user is "user"; the home directory is "/home/user". - User-facing "" maps to "/home/user". - Avoid sudo, installation, destructive commands, GUI launches, network access, and any evaluator behavior that modifies the VM. # Verification Contract - Treat proposal.evaluation_requirements_text as the deterministic contract for proposal.success_criteria. - Use proposal.dependency_chain to check that final artifacts are grounded in required source information, not merely plausible final outputs. - Prefer file or command checks over visual checks. Do not merely check that file exists; check content, structure, formatting, metadata, or state. - Use rule-based verification whenever files or commands can fully express the success conditions. Add VLM judgment only for indispensable visual or otherwise unparsable state; VLM-only verification is allowed only when no reliable programmatic check exists. # Getter Rules Allowed getter types are vm_file, vm_command_line, and empty. - vm_file.path must be an absolute VM path. - vm_command_line.command must be list of arguments, not shell string. - Use empty when the expected answer can be hard-coded inside the rule function. # Rule Function Rules - Each rule item contains complete Python function named call_rule_judge_N. - Signature: def call_rule_judge_N(result, expected, **options) -> float: - Return float in [0.0, 1.0]; catch exceptions and return 0.0. - Do not directly open VM paths in code. Use getter-provided local result or expected paths, or parse stdout from vm_command_line. - Decompose scoring into meaningful subgoals when possible, so partial progress receives partial credit but only dependency-faithful completion receives 1.0. # Output Return JSON: { "verification": { "need_rule_judge": true, "need_vlm_judge": false, "vlm_desc": "When enabled, describe the exact visual evidence to inspect.", "rule_items": [ "result_getter": {}, "expected_getter": {"type": "empty"}, "code": "def call_rule_judge_1(result, expected, **options):n return 0.0" { } ] } } 45 G.

sections.title: INSTRUCTION QUALITY REVIEW PROMPT
sections.content: Instruction Quality Review Prompt (Simplified Version) # Role and Objective Critique every GUI task proposal and accept at most target_count. Use rationality_score as the primary quality signal; require strong verification and answer-isolation scores. Treat complexity_score as descriptive only. # Review Dimensions - Grounding and feasibility: the task is reachable from config, uses only initialized related_apps and used_files, and makes no hidden assumptions. - Clarity and realism: instruction is concise user goal rather than tutorial; it identifies exact paths, objects, destinations, output shape, and constraints. - Verification sufficiency: success_criteria and evaluation_requirements_text are complete, mutually consistent, and precise enough to implement without access to exploration screenshots. - Answer isolation: instruction does not reveal values that must be obtained by reading, counting, comparing, transforming, or inspecting source material. - Rule grounding: require stable deterministic checks whenever VM files or command output capture the condition; file existence alone is insufficient. Visual-only conditions require an explicit, task-specific VLM rubric. - Safety and stability: reject destructive or irreversible state changes, package installation, external side effects such as messaging, subjective-only goals, and current web/date dependencies. - Data and config fit: sampled artifacts are used when relevant, target paths and application state match config, and existing files are edited in place unless the goal explicitly requests new output. - Diversity: avoid recent task patterns and filename-only variants recorded in application memory. - If multiple applications are genuinely required, dependency_chain must state verifiable source-to-operation-to-target dependency; do not reward unrelated parallel actions merely for involving more applications. # Scoring and Selection Use integer scores from 1 (unusable) to 5 (excellent). - rationality_score: realism, reachability, grounding, safety, and unambiguity. - complexity_score: planning horizon, transformations, precision, and state. - success_criteria_score: completeness and consistency of the verification contract. - instruction_leakage_score: withholding derived answers while remaining clear. Reject low-quality proposals directly. For each rejection, provide short machine-readable reason and actionable suggested_repair. Rank accepted items by rationality_score, using verification and leakage scores as quality gates. # Output Return valid JSON only: { "proposal_scores": [{ "proposal_id": "p01", "critic_scores": { "rationality_score": 1, "complexity_score": 1, "success_criteria_score": 1, "instruction_leakage_score": 1 }, "rationale": "brief score rationale" }], "accepted": ["p01"], "rejected": [{ "proposal_id": "p02", "reason": "short_reason", "suggested_repair": "concise actionable feedback" }], "coverage_summary": {} } 46 G.7 EVALUATOR QUALITY REVIEW PROMPT Evaluator Quality Review Prompt (Simplified Version) # Role and Objective Critique and score the existing verification for one accepted task. Do not rewrite the instruction, proposal metadata, or evaluator code. Decide whether repair is required and give concise feedback for evaluator regeneration. # Review Dimensions - Coverage: verify every critical condition in instruction, success_criteria, and evaluation_requirements_text, including target identity, values, counts, order, formatting, metadata, negative conditions, and any genuine dependency. - Getter correctness: require concrete absolute VM paths consistent with the task. vm_file result is local cached file path that rule code must open or parse; vm_command_line result is stdout text. - Structural validity: inspect the internal content or application-specific structure that proves completion, rather than file existence or size alone. - False-positive resistance: initial, empty, partial, stale, wrong-path, wrong-file, or superficially similar states should receive low reward. - Evidence matching: use deterministic rule checks when files or commands capture the condition; use VLM evidence only for indispensable visual or unparsable state. - Safety and determinism: avoid network access, package installation, destructive commands, current external facts, and hidden assumptions. # Scoring and Repair Use integer scores from 1 (unusable) to 5 (excellent). Treat evaluator_quality_score as primary and use coverage_score, getter_correctness_score, structure_validation_score, and false_positive_resistance_score to explain it. Set repair_required to true whenever schema/static validation or initial-state preflight failed, or whenever the review finds material quality defect. Name the missing check, incorrect getter semantics, unsafe behavior, or false-positive path in suggested_repair. # Output Return valid JSON only: { "evaluator_scores": { "evaluator_quality_score": 1, "coverage_score": 1, "getter_correctness_score": 1, "structure_validation_score": 1, "false_positive_resistance_score": 1 }, "rationale": "brief score rationale", "repair_required": true, "rejected": { "reason": "short_reason", "suggested_repair": "concise actionable feedback" } }
